The 7-day binding policy is new evidence that overrides the settled 30-day decision, so I reopened the frozen v2 spec (preserving it under history) rather than editing it silently.

What changed:
- D1 (30 days) is superseded — the policy is binding and the owner confirmed they can't waive it, so retention is now capped at 7 days.
- The existing purge implementation already re-evaluates every record against the current parameter on each scheduled run, and you confirmed the new cap takes effect at the first scheduled purge after deployment — no migration script, immediate purge, or backlog deadline needed. I recorded that as its own decision so it isn't lost.
- R1 now targets 7 days with day6/day8 boundary fixtures (mirroring the day29/day31 pattern you used for 30 days, avoiding an exact-day ambiguity).
- R2 (preserve purge logic/deployment, only touch the parameter and boundary tests) still holds — nothing about that changed.

Since only this dataset is affected, it has no copies elsewhere, and both the cap and its rollout timing are now settled with no open blockers, the spec is validated again at v3. I'm moving straight into plan mode next, as this workflow does once a spec is ready — no separate approval needed to start planning.

# Internal dataset retention

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v3
Frozen: true
Type: Engineering
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Problem Statement

Keep a bounded investigation history in the existing internal dataset, now under a newly supplied binding internal policy capping identifiable-record retention at 7 days.

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Retain for 30 days | Decided: owner previously chose 30 days | Superseded by D3 — binding policy now caps retention below this value | superseded |
| D2 | Keep existing purge implementation and deployment process; change only the retention parameter and its boundary tests | Decided: owner's settled scope | None | resolved |
| D3 | Retention for this dataset's identifiable records is capped at 7 days | Observed: binding internal policy document supplied caps retention at 7 days; Decided: owner confirms they cannot waive the policy and adopts the 7-day cap | None — the cap is mandatory, not discretionary | resolved |
| D4 | The 7-day parameter takes effect at the first scheduled purge after the existing approved deployment process; no separate migration, immediate purge, or backlog deadline is required | Decided: owner's stated rollout approach; Observed: existing purge job re-evaluates every record against the current parameter on each scheduled run, so the normal cycle naturally sweeps records older than 7 days once deployed | None | resolved |

## Decision History

- D1 ("Retain for 30 days", basis: Decided — owner previously chose 30 days) was legitimate when made and is preserved here. It is superseded by D3 because a newly supplied binding internal policy caps retention below 30 days, and the owner lacks authority to waive that policy.

## Critique Reconciliation

_None._

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Set the existing purge parameter to 7 days | Parameter is 7; a day-6-old record remains after purge and a day-8-old record is purged | D3 |
| R2 | Preserve purge logic and deployment process | Diff contains only parameter and boundary-test updates | D2 |
| R3 | New parameter takes effect through the existing scheduled purge cycle, with no separate migration | No manual backlog-purge script or one-off migration is added; the first scheduled purge run after deployment applies the 7-day parameter to all existing records | D4 |

## Constraints

Only this dataset is in scope; it has no copies in other stores. No broader rollout is authorized.

## Success Criteria

The deployed purge job enforces a 7-day retention boundary for this dataset going forward, using only the existing purge/deployment mechanism, with no separate migration or manual backlog action.

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide
Edit mechanics for the parameter and boundary-test changes.

### Executor Must Escalate
Any change to purge/deployment behavior, or any request to alter the 7-day cap.

### Executor Must Not Change
The retention duration (fixed by binding policy, not owner-waivable) or the purge/deployment mechanism (D2).

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests
Run the existing purge tests with the parameter set to 7 and day-6/day-8 age fixtures per R1; inspect the diff for R2 (parameter and boundary tests only); confirm no migration/backlog script was added per R3.

### Regression Checks
Re-run existing purge test suite to confirm only the retention value and its boundary fixtures changed.

### Failure Signals
Unexpected retention beyond 7 days, early deletion before day 7, out-of-scope changes to purge logic/deployment, or any added migration/backlog mechanism fail validation.

### Verification Methods
Check after the edit, before deployment.

### Feedback Loop Design
A failed check requires correction before completion; no separate cadence beyond the standard test run.

### Known Blind Spots
None identified; dataset has no copies elsewhere, so no cross-store consistency check is needed.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking
None.

### Non-Blocking
None.

### Intentional
None.

## Risks

None beyond standard deployment risk for a parameter/test-only change.
</spec_end_marker_unused>

responses.reply: That matches what's already recorded in the validated v3 spec: R1 sets the parameter to 7 with day-6-remains/day-8-purged as the exact boundary criterion, D2/R2 keep the existing purge logic and deployment process untouched, D4/R3 confirm the change lands through the normal scheduled purge cycle with no migration or backlog step, and D1's superseded 30-day decision plus the reason (binding, non-waivable 7-day policy) are preserved in Decision History. No new requirement or implementation choice is being introduced. Since nothing here changes the settled record, the spec stays Validated at v3 and I'm proceeding straight into plan mode.
